Subject: Q4 launch — temporary capacity surge and co-term question

Hey Sean,

Hope you had a good weekend. Quick one — we have a product launch planned for early Q4 that could triple our inference volume for ~8-10 weeks. Current contract with Redwood is for an annual committed capacity (renewal next May). We need two things clarified so we can budget and get procurement moving: 

- Can Redwood support a short-term burst (3x baseline) for ~2 months with predictable pricing?
- Would we be able to add that burst as a mid-contract amendment and have it co-term with our existing May renewal (i.e., not extend the contract length)?

Procurement also asked about discounts for short-term committed top-ups vs paying purely on overage. I attached a rough forecast (orion_q4_forecast.xlsx).

If you can sketch options (pricing delta, invoicing cadence, any necessary amendment language), that would help us decide between an uplift amendment vs pushing more traffic into the hosted overage model.

Thanks — appreciate a quick call if easier.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Q4 launch — temporary capacity surge and co-term question

Alex — thanks for the forecast, this is a great heads-up. We can absolutely support a burst like this; below are three pragmatic paths so procurement has clear options quickly: 

1) Short-term uplift amendment (recommended)
   - Commit to a fixed additional capacity bucket for 8 weeks.
   - Discount: a time-limited uplift discount (example: 10–15% off list for the burst portion depending on committed tokens).
   - Billing: single amendment that invoices monthly for the uplift; amendment co-terms to your May renewal (no extension).

2) Temporary credits (fast, lower friction)
   - Purchase prepaid burst credits that burn against usage. Less paperwork but no co-term; credits expire at contract renewal.
   - Discount: smaller (5–8%) vs amendment.

3) Overage with caps (minimal legal work)
   - Run on overage rates with a hard usage cap and automatic alerts. No upfront discount, but predictable unit rates.

A couple of notes/questions to finish a formal quote: 
- Do you want billing monthly or consolidated at month-end? (Procurement often prefers monthly invoices to finance@orionai.com.)
- Will the burst be a sustained uplift (same histogram each day) or spiky (short peaks)? That affects batching and unit economics; if spiky we can suggest a slightly higher per-token discount in exchange for commitment.

If you're okay, I can convert option 1 into a one-page amendment and send to procurement for review (I’ll include redline language so legal can fast-track). Want me to proceed?

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Sean / Naomi,

Quick internal note on pricing levers for ORION-4738 based on the forecast:

- For an 8-week committed burst, we should propose a blended uplift rate (annualize the uplift to compute a discount but cap the term to co-term). Practically: annualize the 8-week uplift to a pro-rata annual commitment and offer 12% discount on the uplifted bucket. This keeps it attractive but protects margin.
- Billing: monthly invoicing for the uplift is preferable (finance ask).
- Legal: use a short amendment that specifies start/end dates and explicitly co-terms to May 2027. We should avoid language that creates a new 12-month obligation.
- Commercial sweetener: offer a one-time credits voucher equal to 5% of the uplift spend if they sign the amendment within 72 hours — useful for procurement to justify the concession.

I recommend option 1 (short-term uplift amendment) as Sean outlined. If procurement balks on the co-term, fallback to prepaid credits with a 7% discount.

I can draft numbers for the quote (example price points and invoice samples) if you want — tell me the baseline monthly tokens and the expected peak per day and I’ll run the math.
